symptom: Upfront fare quotes have drifted upward against settled fares over recent months. No pipeline has failed, no alert has fired, and the schema has not changed. Nobody knows why.

root_cause.headline: A new vendor ID '7' appeared in the data starting December 2024, causing the model to score these rows as unknown.
root_cause.change_description: The vendor_id column in the raw.yellow_trips dataset started including the new value '7' from December 2024 onwards. This new value was not seen in the training data and thus was not encoded for model prediction.
root_cause.mechanism: The presence of a new vendor ID resulted in categorical feature mismatch, affecting the encoded features is_vendor_cmt, is_vendor_curb, and is_vendor_myle, with none of these indicators firing for the new vendor ID, causing the model to categorize these data points as unknown.
root_cause.why_monitors_missed_it: Conventional monitors did not fire because schema, freshness, and volume checks remained stable. The unique count monitor was the only one that noticed a new categorical level, but it did not attribute it to model scoring logic disruption.

impact.estimator_note: did_* nets out the control model's advantage from having more and fresher training data, measured on segments with no encoding defect. Report did_attributable_dollars as the headline; it is the stricter of the two estimates.

root_cause.recommended_fix: Update the feature engineering pipeline to handle the new vendor ID '7' and retrain the model with data that includes this new category.
proven: A new vendor ID '7' appeared starting December 2024 as per vendor_id profiling.
Feature drift analysis identified feature degradation in segment for vendor ID '7'.
Semantic change in vendor_id explains the change in model performance for these specific rows.
inferred: The model is categorizing these rows as unknown due to missing encoded features for the new vendor ID.
